Time from starting the run until the first response token arrives. Lower feels more responsive.
End-to-end time for this run, including model loading, prompt processing, and generation.
The conversation input and reserved response space available to this run. Older messages may be omitted when the limit is reached.
Earlier conversation messages left out to keep the prompt within the context window.
Input tokens read before the response. Tokens per second measures prompt processing speed; higher is faster.
Sampling controls that shape how varied the response can be. These settings affect output quality, not just speed.
The local model used to produce this response.
Cold starts load a model into memory. Warm starts reuse one that is already loaded; thread count is the effective CPU parallelism.

Save each run to Runs history
Median completion time across the measured runs.
95% of runs completed within this time; useful for spotting slow runs.
Fastest to slowest measured completion time.
Process CPU time over wall time. 100% equals one fully used CPU core, so multi-core work can exceed 100%.
Largest proportional set size (PSS) during this run. PSS estimates shared memory proportionally.
Android device thermal status at the end of the run. Severe or higher stops a profile to protect the device.
Battery reporting is coarse for short profiles. Longer workloads produce more useful readings; current sign follows the device power driver.
Energy-counter change over all measured runs. Availability depends on the device.

Turn speech and recordings into text.
Length of the recording or imported audio that was transcribed.
End-to-end time from starting the run until the completed transcript was available. This includes model loading and decoding.
Time reported by the speech engine while it decoded audio. This can differ from the full run time because setup and app overhead are excluded.
Final-result time divided by audio duration. Below 1× means the transcript completed faster than the audio length.
Number of audio pieces processed. Longer audio may be split into bounded segments before decoding.
Time spent preparing the selected speech model before transcription began.
Effective CPU worker count used by the speech runtime for this run.
Time until the model produced the first audio samples. Lower values make speech feel more responsive.
Time until the app handed the first generated audio samples to Android\'s playback buffer.
Time spent generating speech audio, excluding model loading and playback drain time.
Duration of the WAV audio created for this request.
Synthesis time divided by generated audio duration. Below 1× means audio was generated faster than it plays.
Sample rate and PCM format of the generated WAV file.
Time spent preparing the selected speech model before synthesis began.
Effective CPU worker count used by the speech runtime for this run.
Times Android\'s playback buffer ran short of audio. Zero indicates uninterrupted playback.
Time spent preparing the voice-conditioning representation. A cache hit reuses a previously prepared representation.
Intermediate speech tokens generated before waveform decoding.
Time spent producing intermediate speech tokens.
Time spent converting generated speech tokens into PCM audio samples.
Memory readings captured by the speech runtime. PSS estimates the app\'s proportional share of memory.
